author: C

components.title: Compute probability of no successes
components.what: Calculate (1-0.12)^12 as the probability of zero successes in 12 attempts.

components.title: Complement to get at least one
components.what: Subtract the no-success probability from 1 and convert to a percentage rounded to two decimals.

log.author: C
log.draft:
For an independent trial with a success probability of $p = 0.12$, the probability of failure on any single attempt is:
$$1 - p = 1 - 0.12 = 0.88$$

Because the 12 attempts are mutually independent, the probability of obtaining zero successes across all 12 attempts is the product of the individual failure probabilities:
$$P(\text{zero successes}) = (1 - 0.12)^{12} = 0.88^{12} \approx 0.215671155$$

Using the complement rule, the probability of at least one success is:
$$P(\text{at least one success}) = 1 - P(\text{zero successes}) = 1 - 0.88^{12} \approx 1 - 0.215671155 = 0.784328845$$

Converting this value to a percentage:
$$0.784328845 \times 100 \approx 78.4328845\%$$

Rounded to two decimal places, this is $78.43\%$.

Python verification:
```python
p_none = (1 - 0.12) ** 12  # 0.2156711550974861
p_at_least_one = 1 - p_none  # 0.7843288449025139
print(f"{p_at_least_one * 100:.2f}")  # 78.43
```

FINAL: 78.43

No assumptions regarding dependence or varying success probabilities are left open.
